what_it_is: The blocker triad, named the moment the stall appears, in the receipt's BLOCKERS field, while the evidence is warm — never at sign-out, never in prose-only memory. One line: what's stopped, by what cause, who owns it, and the next physical step (the command, the file, the ask location).
what_it_does: Keeps stalls from becoming orphans. A decline that names instead of completing. A merge package that routes instead of waits. A verdict that hands the author a repair list, not a wish. The stall moves to the one who can move it — it never parks on the reviewer, and never parks on Shawn without the protocol remainder named.
why_it_matters: The builder seat (Naya Clarity) hit the self-review prohibition on the confirm/rework verdict for PR #2591 and declined — naming the blocker (identity: the verdict must come from a non-Clarity seat), the owner (any non-Clarity seat, via a visible claimability gate prepended to the brief), and the path (fact-pack head pin 98426c3b…3abe0 verified current, re-pin at action time, run the post-repair-bytes check). The receipt closes: 'it names the blocker, not a completion' (twelve-lane-receipts/gap-t0776-lane9.md). The opposite: the #2533 phantom claim — the single merge blocker for milestone 1, sitting in the claimed queue 18+ minutes with no sign-in naming it — no owner visibly working it, no path proposed, the queue silently losing the most important brief in the system. And at PR level: the t0712 seat disclosed that an unverified 'all handles dead' claim would have sent the author chasing seven ghosts instead of fixing four real ones — a vague NEEDS_WORK with no named handles, no owner, no path is a complaint, not a blocker.
key_rules: Every stall names three things — the blocker, its owner, the unblock path — or it is an orphan.
Name the triad the moment the stall appears, in the receipt's BLOCKERS field, while the evidence is warm — never at sign-out, never in prose-only memory.
Exactly one named owner — a lane, a seat, a gate. Ownership by everyone is ownership by no one.
The owner knows the next physical step: the command, the file, the ask location.
Never write 'waiting on Shawn' without the protocol remainder — the exact thing only his word unlocks, and why no seat can move it.
If you are the wrong seat, decline and re-file with the gate visible. The next seat gets your starting kit, not your residue.
A vague NEEDS_WORK with no named handles, no owner, no path is a complaint, not a blocker.
test: Does this blocker name its cause in one sentence I could act on — or does it trail off after 'waiting on...'?
Is there exactly one named owner — a lane, a seat, a gate — or is ownership everyone's (which is no one's)?
Does the owner know the next physical step: the command, the file, the ask location?
If Shawn is the owner: did I name the protocol remainder — the exact thing his word unlocks — and did I verify it is genuinely his gate, not my avoidance?
If no owner exists: have I routed it (dispatcher, board ask, lane assignment) instead of parking it silently?
A stall with no triad past the audit's window: is it already back in the queue? If not, why not?

enforcement.real: The claim-liveness audit in the night-dispatcher: no sign-in naming the brief and claim older than 60 minutes → PHANTOM CLAIM returned to queue; sign-in with no receipt after 6 ticks → STALE. The receipt BLOCKERS convention: 59 receipt files carry a BLOCKERS field (grep-verified). The consolidated blocker list pattern: WHY / SOLUTION / OWNER / STATE. Board Protocol asks: cross-seat routing with the exact next step named. The two-seat rule: the missing independent seat is a structural blocker that cannot be wished away.
enforcement.proposed: No automatic escalation exists for blockers whose state sits OWED beyond N ticks — owed items live in receipts and the consolidated list, re-ranked by the director pass, but nothing mechanical forces them up. Named as the gap, not a fiction.
